scope: Current mfe-base compatibility with BFF CES migration; source/contract inspection and existing tests only

findings.title: Current sample login and nonblank tile admission already fit normalized contract
findings.classification: confirmed source relationship; sample compatibility predicted by source
findings.evidence: handleUser decodes entitlementsToken JSON and attaches response entities unchanged. Entry compares names from returned drawer entity arrays. Captured CES entity and all 41 returned CES tile entity arrays use RATAN_ENTITLEMENT_RULE. All returned CES subjects are nonblank and match the returned CES entity subjects. X_RATANONE is absent from captured entities.
findings.consequence: No blanket login API or decoder replacement is required for this sample.
findings.next_action: Retain normalized entity/subject/action contract and validate login, relogin, validate, and extend with mixed EMS2/CES samples.

findings.title: Replace legacy tile re-evaluation with a consistent normalized CES admission decision
findings.classification: required compatibility change for supported CES configurations; conditional runtime impact
findings.evidence: BFF checks entitlementAppFeature, but drawer subject remains ems2_subject. Base requires nonempty legacy subject and checks only first matching entity. Source X_RATANONE fallback is scalar-only and does not map CES. CSV tile192 has blank feature and subject, but is absent from this login capture. Other differing-feature and multiple-app cases remain configuration boundaries, not observed sample failures.
findings.consequence: A BFF-admitted CES tile can open from drawer yet fail deep-link or saved-workspace retention if old subject is blank or differs from granted CES feature.
findings.next_action: Use exact membership in the current BFF-authorized drawer for CES admission, or return an explicit normalized grant decision/feature contract and share one validator across launch and workspace paths. Preserve template and missing-configuration rules. Remove/isolate the legacy X_RATANONE fallback only with EMS2 compatibility evidence.

findings.title: Expose and audit the four CES tile configuration fields
findings.evidence: Columns and new-row defaults omit entitlementSource, entitlementAppId, entitlementAppName, entitlementAppFeature. Audit view omits these fields. Existing fetched rows are cloned and spread, so supplied metadata survives an ordinary edit or verify. BFF /tile/data returns full ApplicationTile including CES properties. No CSV upload/export UI exists in inspected ts/tsx source.
findings.consequence: Admin cannot create or change CES routing or review these routing values during maker/checker audit. Ordinary current edits do not establish a source reset defect.
findings.next_action: Add source selector and app ID/name/features controls, conditional validation consistent with BFF, explicit defaults, displayed maker/checker/audit fields, and payload preservation assertions. Extend external CSV consumers only when they exist.

findings.title: Align shared TypeScript models with mixed-provider nullable metadata
findings.classification: required contract maintenance; no current runtime failure established
findings.evidence: CES normalized entity id, applicationName, roleId and roleName are null. Subject id, action id and action entitlementId are also null in the capture. Current Entity/Subject/Action interfaces require legacy nonnull fields. Subject and Tile interfaces omit entitlementSource. Only the admin role helper consumes roleName for access decisions in inspected base source; captured admin remains EMS2 FMO PORTAL ADMIN with RATAN_PROD.
findings.consequence: Current types misdescribe real responses and encourage false role-based assumptions.
findings.next_action: Add provider union and source markers; make legacy identifiers/role metadata nullable or optional. Keep admin ownership role separate from CES effective feature/action grants. Do not infer roles from appName:null token keys.
